logs: Review of records: Not ready. All suites pass, but they miss confirmed defects. One blocker: closure_update shares a single mutable 'stages' dict across every new closure in a process, so a second new closure inherits the first one's stages. There are 14 majors. lock_seen writes back an unlocked copy of the lock, which revives a released lock entry and overwrites a takeover. Run and decision read-modify-writes take no flush.lock. The spec approval misses added spec files and raises on deleted ones. settle_decision accepts topology=banana, repeated non-repeatable keys, and 'skip' for any blocked reason. Bare decision ids count closed cycles. flush raises on a corrupt lock.json, never commits deletions while reporting 'clean', and fails outright when git has no identity. P3SEAM-15's re-freeze check has two holes. StoreBusy and StoreCorrupt sit under StoreRefused, against the plan. The holdout refusal is over-broad. Evidence lookup branches are untested. AU-S2-06, AU-P2-03 and AU-S2-04 are marked fixed while the spec duplication remains. 17 minors cover outcome statuses, a weak test, partial writes, flush staging, the note shape, patch_id shape, the run-record id, and event fields. Check output: tools/check.py 30/30 PASS. pytest 836 passed, 1 skipped (118 s). node universal.test.mjs 27 pass, 0 fail. spec_lint 0 problems. findings.py build: 540 findings (361 fixed, 69 left-for-builder, 4 not-fixed, 105 open, 1 rejected), open by severity 1 blocker, 58 major, 119 minor, by-package lists written. No failures in files owned by other units. No __pycache__ under next/plugins before or after (the pre-existing tests/ and tools/ caches date from 16:19 and are not mine). still_open.problem: New, caused by the S3R-records-9 fix. commit_rels is filtered by 'git diff --cached --name-only -z', which detects renames by default and then prints only the new name. When a tracked state file is deleted and a similar one added in the same flush (a story or spec file renamed or renumbered), the deleted path drops out of the commit and the deletion stays staged ('D '). Every later flush then returns state 'failed': 'git add -A -- <path>' refuses a path that is in neither the index nor the worktree ('pathspec did not match any files'). Probe: rename stories/E-1/S-1.01.md to S-1.02.md. The second flush is 'committed' with files [S-1.02.md] only, the third is 'failed'. With the old commit list (all valid rels) the same probe committed both paths and the next flush was clean, so this is a regression. A deletion staged by a killed flush hits the same add failure; that was there before this round.
still_open.proposed_fix: Add --no-renames to the diff --cached that builds commit_rels. Stage existing paths with 'git add -A --' and paths gone from the worktree with 'git rm --cached -q --ignore-unmatch --'. I tried this in a scratch copy: the rename and staged-deletion probes both commit and the next flush is clean, and test_state_commits.py still passes. Add tests for a renamed committed story (state committed, tree clean, next flush clean) and for a committed file whose deletion was already staged.

still_open.problem: New, caused by the S3R-records-C1-1 fix. When flush.lock is busy, lock_release keeps the entry and returns normally, without StoreBusy. Plan records.md 3 says 'StoreBusy after wait', and the docstring was changed to match the new code. Callers cannot tell 'busy' from 'nothing matched'. Probe with flush.lock held by another process: 'vsdd lock release --force' took 3.02 s and exited 0 with {ok: true, released: [], holder: null}, while lock.json still held the entry and its run was live. Without --force, the caller's own entry is reported as 'another session's live run holds the lock'. The SessionEnd caller (wait=0.5) gets the same silent result.
still_open.proposed_fix: Keep the bounded per-entry wait. After writing the kept entries, raise StoreBusy carrying the released entries whenever an entry was kept because run_end was busy. In cmd_lock, catch StoreBusy and exit 1 with an error saying a flush is running, never holder null. Test: with flush.lock held, lock_release(wait=0.5) raises StoreBusy within about 0.6 s with lock.json unchanged, and 'lock release --force' exits non-zero.
